intro: Bedford's story stretches from colonial farmland to a modern town that is home to Hanscom Air Force Base and the Bedford VA. Here are some highlights from its first 300 years.

facts.title: Two Brothers Rocks
facts.text: Governor John Winthrop and Deputy Governor Thomas Dudley divided land along the Concord River. Two boulders near the river, later called the Two Brothers Rocks, are said to mark the boundary between their farms.
facts.imageAlt: PLACEHOLDER: Two large boulders near the Concord River
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: The Job Lane House
facts.text: The Job Lane House, a farmhouse built in the early 1700s, survives today as a museum that shows how Bedford families lived across three centuries.
facts.imageAlt: PLACEHOLDER: The Job Lane House, a colonial farmhouse
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: Bedford Is Incorporated
facts.text: On September 23, 1729, Bedford was incorporated as a town, formed from parts of Concord and Billerica so that residents could have a church and meetinghouse closer to home.
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: The Old Burying Ground
facts.text: Bedford's oldest cemetery holds the graves of many early settlers and Revolutionary War soldiers, with slate headstones dating to the town's first decades.
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: Bedford Minutemen March to Concord
facts.text: On April 19, 1775, Bedford's Minutemen gathered at Fitch Tavern before marching to Concord. Captain Jonathan Wilson was killed later that day in the fighting along the road back toward Boston.
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: The Bedford Flag
facts.text: The Bedford Flag, carried by Bedford's Minutemen in 1775, is believed to be one of the oldest surviving flags in the United States. Its Latin motto, Vince aut Morire, means "Conquer or Die." The original is preserved at the Bedford Free Public Library.
facts.imageAlt: The Bedford Flag: a crimson banner showing an armored arm reaching out of a cloud and gripping a sword, with a gold ribbon bearing the Latin motto Vince aut Morire
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society
facts.imageCredit: Illustration of the Bedford Flag by HoosierMan1816, Wikimedia Commons (public domain)

facts.title: The Railroad Arrives
facts.text: Railroad service connected Bedford to Boston and nearby towns. The restored Bedford Depot area is now a gateway to the Minuteman Bikeway.
facts.imageAlt: PLACEHOLDER: The historic Bedford railroad depot
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: The Bedford VA Hospital Opens
facts.text: A veterans hospital opened in Bedford, beginning a long tradition of caring for those who served. Today it is the Edith Nourse Rogers Memorial Veterans Hospital.
facts.imageAlt: PLACEHOLDER: Brick buildings of the Bedford VA campus
facts.source: DRAFT – to be verified with the Bedford Historical Society

facts.title: Hanscom Field
facts.text: An airfield opened on the Bedford border in the early 1940s and was later named for aviator Laurence G. Hanscom. Hanscom Air Force Base has been part of the community ever since.
